title: If Statements
story: if runs a command and looks at its exit status. Zero means yes. [ ] is a command that tests things.
goal: If the first argument is greater than 10 print big, otherwise print small.
hints:
if [ "$1" -gt 10 ]; then
  echo big
else
  echo small
fi
socratic: Why do the spaces inside [ ] matter?
What does the exit status of a command mean to if?
explain: In one sentence: what did you learn from “If Statements”?
solution:
if [ "$1" -gt 10 ]; then
  echo big
else
  echo small
fi
alt: if (( $1 > 10 )); then echo big; else echo small; fi
